/-!
# Erdős Problem 57

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/57](https://www.erdosproblems.com/57)
- [ErHa66] Erdős, P. and Hajnal, A., *On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems*.
  Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1966), 61-99.
- [LiMo20] Liu, Hong and Montgomery, Richard, *A solution to Erdős and Hajnal's odd cycle problem*.
  arXiv:2010.15802 (2020).
-/

namespace Erdos57

/--
If $G$ is a graph with infinite chromatic number and $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ are lengths of the odd
cycles of $G$ then $\sum \frac{1}{a_i} = \infty$.

Conjectured by Erdős and Hajnal [ErHa66], and solved by Liu and Montgomery [LiMo20].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_57 :
    ∀ {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ →
      ¬ Summable (fun (a : G.oddCycleLengths) ↦ 1 / (a : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos57

findings.description: The theorem docstring (line 36) cites [ErHa66] as the source of the odd-cycle conjecture. That paper's Problem 7.8 concerns reciprocals of all cycle lengths, without restricting to odd lengths. The odd-cycle conjecture is explicitly stated in Erdős's 1981 paper. This is a citation slip only; the Lean proposition is faithful to the odd-cycle problem.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős–Hajnal, On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems (1966), Problem 7.8, p. 78, defines N using all circuit lengths: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1966-07.pdf. Erdős, Problems and results in graph theory (1981), §5, p. 338, states the infinite-chromatic-number conjecture with lengths 2r+1: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-20.pdf. Liu–Montgomery, arXiv:2010.15802v2, §§1.1–1.2, explicitly distinguishes the 1966 all-cycle question from the 1981 odd-cycle question.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a reference to Erdős, Problems and results in graph theory (1981), pp. 331–341, especially p. 338, and cite it instead of [ErHa66] in the theorem docstring. Retain [ErHa66] only as background for the earlier all-cycle version. No change to the Lean proposition is needed.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses `chromaticNumber = ⊤` and non-summability of a real-valued function indexed by the set of odd-cycle lengths, rather than an infinite cardinal chromatic number and an increasing reciprocal series whose sum is +∞.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Mathlib's chromatic number equals ⊤ exactly when no finite proper coloring exists. The subtype `G.oddCycleLengths` contains each distinct odd-cycle length once, and every such length is at least 3. Thus all reciprocal terms are positive. Reindexing by the indicator function on ℕ preserves summability, and non-summability of this nonnegative series is equivalent to its cutoff partial sums tending to +∞. The same equivalence holds along any bijective enumeration of the length set, including its increasing enumeration. Both the chromatic-number equivalence and the summability/divergence equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in the sole theorem. The `research solved` tag agrees with Liu–Montgomery's positive solution. The scratch file compiles successfully; its checks have no sorry dependencies. Tests include empty and small finite graphs, the triangle's odd-cycle spectrum {3}, exclusion of empty/backtracking walks as cycles, and the complete graph on ℕ as a witness satisfying the infinite-chromatic hypothesis. The live erdosproblems.com/57 page remained inaccessible behind Cloudflare despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the mathematical claim and status were verified from the primary literature instead.
